title: Three writes
description:
Print this with **three** separate `write` system calls, one per line, each with its own label and its own length worked out by `equ $ - label`:

```
Name:  Grace Hopper
Born:  1906
Known for:  the first compiler
```

Then exit with code 0. Remember that `rax` holds the result of each system call, so set it to 1 again before the next `write`.

starter.main.asm:
global  _start

        section .data
line1:  db      "Name:  Grace Hopper", 10
len1    equ     $ - line1

        section .text
_start:
        mov     eax, 1
        mov     edi, 1
        lea     rsi, [rel line1]
        mov     edx, len1
        syscall

        mov     eax, 60
        xor     edi, edi
        syscall

solution.main.asm:
global  _start

        section .data
line1:  db      "Name:  Grace Hopper", 10
len1    equ     $ - line1
line2:  db      "Born:  1906", 10
len2    equ     $ - line2
line3:  db      "Known for:  the first compiler", 10
len3    equ     $ - line3

        section .text
_start:
        mov     eax, 1
        mov     edi, 1
        lea     rsi, [rel line1]
        mov     edx, len1
        syscall

        mov     eax, 1
        mov     edi, 1
        lea     rsi, [rel line2]
        mov     edx, len2
        syscall

        mov     eax, 1
        mov     edi, 1
        lea     rsi, [rel line3]
        mov     edx, len3
        syscall

        mov     eax, 60
        xor     edi, edi
        syscall

hints: Give each line its own label and `equ $ - label` right after it, so each length counts only that line.
Each `write` needs `eax` = 1, `edi` = 1, `rsi` = the line and `edx` = its length set again: the previous system call left its result in `rax`.
rules: Use three write system calls and the exit call.

Born:  1906
Known for:  the first compiler
